intel.text: There are no public roads or parking lots in the park; vehicles are staged at the gateway airports in Nain or Kuujjuaq. Confirm secure storage with local air charter providers before arrival.

intel.text: Cellular service is non-existent within the park boundaries. Satellite phones or GPS messengers are standard requirements for all independent parties.

intel.text: Fuel is not available for purchase within the park; all supplies are managed through the Torngat Mountains Base Camp. Expeditions must carry all necessary reserves for the duration of their trip.

intel.text: Access is strictly limited by the timing of sea ice break-up, typically occurring in mid-to-late July. Earlier attempts are often blocked by pack ice in Saglek Bay.

intel.text: Parks Canada strongly recommends an Inuit Bear Guard; it is not a blanket requirement for all independent visitors. Commercial operators may impose additional requirements. Independent visitors must be self-reliant and follow registration and polar bear safety guidance.

travel_plan.vehicle: No road access; travel is exclusively by boat, aircraft, or on foot. Verify luggage weight limits with charter airlines.

intel.text: There is no cellular or internet service within the park. Satellite phones and PLBs are mandatory for all independent expeditions for safety reporting.

intel.text: The travel season is restricted to July and August. Ice break-up on the Thomsen River usually occurs in late June, and winter conditions return rapidly in September.

intel.text: There are no roads or parking facilities in Aulavik. Vehicle logistics are limited to airport transfers in Inuvik or quad-trailer transport in Sachs Harbour.

intel.text: There are no parking lots within the park; long-term parking is typically arranged at private air charter bases in Norman Wells or Tulita. Travelers should verify security and fees with their specific flight provider before arrival.

intel.text: Mobile coverage is non-existent within the park boundaries and throughout most of the Sahtu region. Satellite communication devices are the standard for backcountry safety and emergency check-ins.

intel.text: Fuel for stoves or expedition equipment must be secured in Norman Wells before chartering into the park. There are no retail services or supply depots once you depart the gateway towns.

intel.text: Access is almost exclusively by floatplane or ski-plane as there is no road network connecting to the park. Hikers arriving via the Canol Heritage Trail must be prepared for extremely strenuous self-supported travel.

travel_plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles cannot reach the park; transport is limited to specialized bush planes. Check with air carriers regarding strict weight limits for gear.

travel_plan.arrival: Arrive in Fort Simpson via Highway 1 or regional flight, visit the Parks Canada Visitor Centre for mandatory orientation, and finalize gear with your outfitter.

intel.text: The main parking lot at the Interpretive Centre serves as the hub for all trails. It can fill during July and August afternoons, so mid-morning arrival is advised.
intel.title: Arrival Logistics

intel.text: The Greenwich Dunes Trail features crushed gravel and a floating boardwalk. It is generally accessible, but heavy rains can occasionally cause soft spots near the pond edges.
intel.title: Trail Surfaces

intel.text: The nearest fuel and full-service grocery stores are located in St. Peters Bay or Morell. There are no convenience services within the National Park boundaries.
intel.title: Nearby Services

intel.text: Signal is reliable near the Interpretive Centre but may fade as you move toward the dunes. Do not rely on GPS for finding trailhead markers; use the official park maps.
intel.title: Network Coverage

intel.text: The Interpretive Centre and washroom facilities have specific seasonal dates, typically operating from June to September. Outside of these months, the trails remain open but services are unavailable.
intel.title: Seasonal Facilities

travel_plan.vehicle: Any standard rental car is suitable for the well-maintained paved roads leading to Greenwich. No off-road capability is required.

travel_plan.arrival: Pick up rental vehicle at Charlottetown Airport (YYG) and acquire groceries in the city before heading 30 minutes north to the park.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes from Charlottetown to Cavendish; conditions vary by traffic.
days.note: Cavendish is the busiest sector; arrive early to secure a location near the beach.

stops.detail: Walk the iconic red sandstone cliffs and white sand beaches that characterize the island's northern shore.
stops.name: Cavendish Beach

stops.detail: Explore the farm and landscapes that inspired L.M. Montgomery's classic novels, located just outside the park boundary.
stops.name: Green Gables Heritage Place

days.title: Red Cliffs and Literary Landscapes

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for travel to the Greenwich peninsula; conditions vary.
days.note: The Greenwich sector is geographically separated from Cavendish; allow extra transit time.

stops.detail: Cross the parabolic dunes via a floating boardwalk to reach one of the most significant sand systems in North America.
stops.name: Greenwich Dunes Trail

stops.detail: Cycle or walk along this paved coastal path for uninterrupted views of the Gulf of Saint Lawrence.
stops.name: Gulf Shore Way

days.title: Dunes and Salt Marshes

days.driving: Allow 30-45 minutes between Stanhope and Cavendish; conditions vary.
days.note: Pace your visit to enjoy the local seafood markets in nearby North Rustico.

stops.detail: Visit the quieter eastern end of the park to see the Covehead Harbour Lighthouse and active fishing wharves.
stops.name: Stanhope Cape Beach

stops.detail: View the historic Queen Anne Revival-style hotel and the surrounding freshwater pond ecosystems.
stops.name: Dalvay-by-the-Sea

days.title: Estuaries and Historic Harbors

travel_plan.goldenHour: Covehead Harbour for sunset views of the lighthouse against the red sand dunes, varying by the time of year.

intel.text: Main parking lots at Cavendish Beach fill quickly on warm weekends. Consider using the shuttle services if active or parking at secondary trailheads like Dunelands.
intel.title: Cavendish Beach Capacity

intel.text: Most areas of the park have good cellular reception due to the proximity of local towns. Remote sections of the Greenwich dunes may have weaker signals.
intel.title: Reliable Coastal Signal

intel.text: Fuel stations are frequent in Cavendish and North Rustico. Ensure you have enough for the longer drive to the Greenwich sector where services are limited.
intel.title: Gateway Services

intel.text: Full services including washrooms and visitor centers typically operate from June through September. Limited access is available in the shoulder season.
intel.title: Seasonal Operations

intel.text: Walking on the dunes is strictly prohibited to prevent erosion. Always use the provided boardwalks and designated beach access paths.
intel.title: Dune Protection

travel_plan.vehicle: Standard passenger cars are ideal for the paved park roads; bicycles are highly recommended for the Gulf Shore Way.

travel_plan.arrival: Arrive at Williams Lake (YWL), rent a high-clearance vehicle, and begin the 5-hour drive west. Stock up on all backcountry supplies in Williams Lake as options are minimal later.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours for mountain pass driving; conditions vary with weather.
days.note: The descent involves steep grades and switchbacks; ensure your vehicle's braking system is in top condition.

stops.detail: The highest point on the Freedom Highway offers views of the transition from the Chilcotin Plateau to the Coast Mountains.
stops.name: Heckman Pass

stops.detail: Experience the famous steep descent into the Bella Coola Valley, stopping at designated pull-outs for views of the Rainbow Range.
stops.name: The Hill

days.title: The Precipice and Valley Vistas

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for trailhead access; conditions vary.
days.note: This is prime grizzly country; carry bear spray and make noise while hiking in dense brush or near creeks.
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from Rainbow Range Trailhead

stops.detail: Hike into this ancient volcanic landscape where the rocks display vibrant shades of red, orange, and yellow.
stops.name: Rainbow Range

stops.detail: Walk through vast alpine meadows that bloom with wildflowers in late July and early August.
stops.name: McCauley Meadows

days.title: Alpine Colors and Volcanic Peaks

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes for valley floor transit; conditions vary.
days.note: Salmon spawning season usually begins in August, attracting significant wildlife activity to the river corridor.

stops.detail: Visit the river banks where grizzly bears often congregate during the salmon spawn in late summer.
stops.name: Atnarko River

stops.detail: Explore the lower valley's lush cedar forests and take a short walk to the viewing platform over the rushing creek.
stops.name: Burnt Bridge Creek

days.title: River Corridors and Ancient Forests

travel_plan.goldenHour: Heckman Pass summit provides an unobstructed view of the Coast Range peaks catching the last light of the day.

intel.text: Parking areas at Heckman Pass and the Rainbow Range are gravel lots that rarely fill to capacity but lack paved markings. Park clearly to allow others room to maneuver.
intel.title: Wilderness Trailheads

intel.text: Expect zero cellular service once you leave the immediate vicinity of Anahim Lake or Bella Coola. Satellite communication devices are recommended for any backcountry travel.
intel.title: Remote Dead Zones

intel.text: The stretch of Highway 20 through the park has no services. Fuel up in Anahim Lake or Bella Coola to ensure you can navigate the steep mountain grades safely.
intel.title: Gap Planning

intel.text: Heckman Pass can receive snow at any time of year, and high alpine trails may remain snow-covered until mid-July. Always check the BC Highway DriveBC reports.
intel.title: Snow and Mud Season

intel.text: Significant portions of the road through the park are gravel and steep. Check rental agreements for restrictions on driving unpaved mountain passes like 'The Hill'.
intel.title: Unpaved Sections

travel_plan.vehicle: A high-clearance 4WD is strongly recommended for the steep grades of Heckman Pass and accessing unpaved trailheads safely.
